BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Wattlebridge Buyer Negotiation Playbook, compared with the Seller's update draft and Disclosure Letter

## Points to note before the issue list

1. **The "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim is unverified.** The Seller says its positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened". Nothing on our file supports this. The playbook records that Amelia Frost has given **no written authority** for the 20% cap or the 18-month period. Unless she confirms otherwise in writing, treat every point as open.
2. **The "market context" preamble is the Seller's advocacy, not agreed fact.** Their claims about market caps, baskets, periods and knowledge qualifiers do not change our positions.
3. **The Disclosure Letter supports several of our concerns.** It confirms there is no Bluefen consent, Riverlark has not been repaid, the bonuses are missing from the funds flow, and title rests only on the internal register. Use these admissions in the mark-up.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000), cl 12.1.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and she has not given it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, excess only (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 as a tipping basket.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's figures are five times ours, and the excess-only structure removes the first AUD 250,000 of every valid claim.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion (cl 12.3/13). The Seller also wants that limitation to apply to *all* Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims only.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert 24 months and limit it expressly to general Warranty Claims.**
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" wording would also cut the Fundamental, fraud and indemnity periods.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years. It must sit outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Reinstate a standalone Fundamental regime.**
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. Capping them at 20% defeats the deal's core protection.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express overriding carve-out.**
- **Reason:** This is non-waivable under the playbook. "All Claims of any nature" would purport to protect the Seller against its own fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DL 1.1), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2. Only specific, fairly disclosed matters should qualify the Warranties.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure is expressly rejected in the playbook. It would neutralise the Warranties wholesale.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete cl 8.3.** If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - refer to *Seller* knowledge;
  - name the knowledge persons;
  - include a reasonable-enquiry standard; and
  - never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reason:** A constructive "discoverable" knowledge bar combined with whole-room disclosure removes nearly all warranty protection.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. The consent is "satisfied on delivery" of Bluefen's written consent (cl 3/6.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent, plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Condition before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective consent with conditions satisfied a hard Condition Precedent.** Delete deemed satisfaction on delivery.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m), and DL 2 confirms that neither the consent nor evidence of the conditions has been provided.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release to be provided "following Completion" for about AUD 3.2m outstanding (cl 2/7).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from the Completion funds; and
  - effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require the payout letter, a direct payment line in the funds flow and executed releases at Completion.**
- **Reason:** DL 3 confirms the facility is unrepaid and undischarged. A post-Completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval, and neither is offered.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and similar) included as a specific funds-flow line item or funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Add an express line item (or price deduction) for bonuses plus on-costs, backed by an indemnity.**
- **Reason:** DL 5 confirms the bonuses are excluded and the on-costs are unaddressed. Without this, the liability would silently pass to the Company and therefore to us.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader IP indemnity that covers non-transfer of SOW3 Project Materials and related IP loss, while keeping the SOW3 cure mechanism.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter. Broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and require proof of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment.**
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the IP depends on payment. DL 4 confirms there is no payment receipt or assignment. The AUD 180,000 figure is unverified either way, so do not treat it as the measure of exposure.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - logs preserved;
  - the investigation continued;
  - regular updates before Completion; and
  - protection that holds whatever the investigation finds.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter. Add covenants on log preservation, investigation and updates. Reserve a specific indemnity or warranty for any outcome of the incident.**
- **Reason:** The facts are unresolved (about 1,240 records, with access and notification status unknown). Neither side should assume a breach, harm or notification duty, but the Seller's materiality assertion should not be accepted either. Make no numeric demand.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of each renewal: whether it is unavoidable, terminable or accrued, and its timing.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold open pending diligence.** Request the DD-008/DD-011 detail. Do not accept the ordinary-course label, and do not demand automatic Debt treatment or a price cut.
- **Reason:** DL 8 states nothing about whether the renewals are avoidable or accrued, so neither side's classification is established yet.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One general regime for everything. Limitations apply to "all Claims", and Tax/IP and Title are folded in.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants kept as separate categories, with no hidden override from the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Add a "nothing in cl 12 limits…" carve-out and define each category's regime separately.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's drafting in cl 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5 collapses every protection into the weakest one.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as:
  - ASIC searches;
  - a PPSR search;
  - share certificates;
  - constitution compliance; and
  - board and shareholder approvals.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone. Require independent title evidence as a Completion deliverable, alongside the full Fundamental title warranty.**
- **Reason:** DL 10 concedes the register is only the Seller's internal source and not verification.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers the Tax and IP terms "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP kept OPEN for separate negotiation.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation. Expressly reserve Tax and IP as open.**
- **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed. Our file assumes neither resolution nor unlimited liability, so we should neither concede nor overreach.

---

## Next steps
1. Prepare a buyer mark-up based on the positions above. Treat 25% and 24 months as our live positions, not fallbacks.
2. Reply to Seller counsel noting that we do not accept that any point is "FINAL" or settled at principal level.
3. **If** the team wants to use any fallback, get Amelia Frost's prior written authority first, identifying this specific draft.
4. Send diligence requests covering:
   - Bluefen consent and the cl 11.3 conditions;
   - the Riverlark payout letter and draft releases;
   - bonus on-cost calculations;
   - Ironquay payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment;
   - DD-006 investigation status and logs;
   - Sandbar renewal terms; and
   - independent title searches.
